# Repository Instructions

Follow the repository-wide workflow and safety rules in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).
The project is a Linux VM starter and agent-handoff toolkit, not an application
with a root build pipeline.

## Build and test

The root package requires Node.js 22 or newer. From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci
npm test
npm run lint
npm run format:check
```

`npm test` runs `scripts/validate.sh`, including Bash/Node syntax checks,
ShellCheck, hygiene checks, and infrastructure tests. Root tests are standalone
scripts; run one with `bash tests/<test-name>.sh`, for example:

```sh
bash tests/stage-router-test.sh
```

There is no root build command. `workspace/bridge` is a separate TypeScript
package with its own lockfile:

```sh
cd workspace/bridge
npm ci
npm test
npx tsc --noEmit
```

The bridge test runner starts a local server on port 3999 by default and uses
local credentials under `~/.config/thunderstone-bridge/tokens`. It refuses to
test against port 3847. For a focused Node test, use
`node --test --test-name-pattern="<test name>" scripts/test-bridge.test.mjs`
from `workspace/bridge` with the test server and credentials available.

CI runs on Ubuntu with Node.js 22, installs ShellCheck and tmux, then runs
`npm ci` and `npm test`.

## Architecture

- `scripts/` is the VM operations layer: bootstrap installs prerequisites,
  `resume.sh` safely restores the tmux workspace, and `cursor-worker.sh`
  manages the optional outbound Cursor Cloud worker. `env-run.mjs` provides
  environment loading; `run-task.sh` is the bounded brief-to-Cursor-CLI path.
- `workspace/bridge/` is a separate local MCP mailbox. Its authenticated tools
  create and list handoff tasks, restrict visibility to sender and recipient,
  and allow only the assignee to post a receipt. Tasks and audit data are
  stored under the configured Thunderstone workspace.
- Agent work follows the investigator → implementer → verifier handoff model.
  Versioned receipts and promotion gates are defined in
  [docs/handoff-protocol.md](../docs/handoff-protocol.md); coordination KPIs
  and deterministic pilot gates are in
  [docs/adr-agent-collection-kpis.md](../docs/adr-agent-collection-kpis.md).
- Cursor hooks provide advisory stage routing and handoff metrics. The stage
  signals and safety limits are documented in
  [docs/stage-router.md](../docs/stage-router.md).
- For skill-generated Markdown, follow
  [.github/instructions/copilot-document-generation.instructions.md](instructions/copilot-document-generation.instructions.md)
  and add Copilot metadata only to documents generated by a requested workflow.
- VM agent roles, worker readiness, and mailbox boundaries are documented in
  [docs/agent-collaboration-vm.md](../docs/agent-collaboration-vm.md). A mailbox
  task marked done is not promotion evidence.

## Repository-specific conventions

- Shell scripts use Bash strict mode; `scripts/bootstrap.sh` is the POSIX `sh`
  entry point so it can prepare Bash on a new VM. Keep tests runnable in the
  Linux/Bash environment used by CI.
- Do not source dotenv files as shell code. Use `node scripts/env-run.mjs ...`
  for commands that need project configuration. Injected environment values
  take precedence over secret files, user configuration, `.env.local`, and
  `.env.defaults`; never print or commit credential values.
- Keep concurrent writers in separate worktrees. Do not recursively launch an
  agent from an existing Cursor agent session.
- Receipt duplication is ignored, and implementation success alone does not
  authorize promotion: verifier acceptance and passing validation are both
  required.
- The bridge has an independent dependency manifest and lockfile. Make
  dependency and test changes in `workspace/bridge/` without replacing or
  regenerating the root package lockfile.
